A mortgage is a loan to buy a home. If you stop paying, the lender can
You pay part of the price yourself. This part is called the deposit (in
A bank lends you the rest. You then pay the bank back each month, often
Until you finish, the bank holds a legal claim on the home. That claim
is what makes it a mortgage, not just a loan.
Each monthly payment has two parts:
: this pays back the money you borrowed.
: this is the fee the bank charges for lending.
The bank works out interest on what you still owe. So you pay a lot of
interest at the start, when you owe the most.

Say you borrow £200,000 at 5% interest over 25 years.

shrinks a little. So the interest part shrinks, and more of the payment

By the last few years, almost all of each payment pays off the debt.
A fixed rate stays the same for a set time, often 2 to 5 years. Your
payment stays the same during that time.
A variable rate can rise or fall. It usually follows the central bank's
rate. Your payment moves with it.
When a fixed deal ends, you often move to a higher rate. Many people
then switch to a new deal. This switch is called remortgaging.
